title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v111
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Add adaptive-batching mixed-workload runners, profiling baselines (cold/warm), and a reporting pipeline v111 that exports run metadata and aggregated metrics to BigQuery and the benchmark dashboard.
description:
Motivation: adaptive batching and workload-aware profiling are key to reducing per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs. This PR adds a new set of benchmark-lab runners that exercise mixed chat/completion/embedding traffic shapes, records cold-start and steady-state profiling baselines, and wires a reporting pipeline (v111) to export aggregated metrics for the dashboard and long-term analysis.

What this PR does: 
- New representative workload runners: mixed_workload_runner.py (concurrent chat/completion/embedding scenarios) and a lightweight runner harness for batch/stream modes.
- Profiling baselines: capture cold-start walltime, kv-cache warmup, GPU memory footprints, and per-token latency percentiles. Baselines stored in profiling/baselines/v111/.
- Reporting pipeline v111: config and templates to ingest runner outputs, normalize tags (model, quantization, sequence_length, batch_size), compute per-run aggregates, and export to BigQuery + S3. Includes alert-friendly fields for regressions.
- CI integration: add pipeline job that runs a smoke mixed-workload for PRs and uploads summary artifacts to CI storage.
- Docs: benchmark-lab/README.md updated with runner examples and how to reproduce baselines locally.

Checklist:
- [x] Add runners and test harness
- [x] Capture profiling baselines (cold/warm) and example artifacts
- [x] Implement reporting pipeline templates and BigQuery export mappings
- [x] Add CI smoke test and artifact upload
- [x] Documentation updates and quickstart example

Notes and links: 
- Related Linear: ENG-3124 (adaptive-batching rollout), ENG-3187 (benchmark dashboard metrics schema)
- Temporary SUP issue: SUP-1423 tracked a bug in the earlier pipeline that dropped sequence_length; this PR canonicalizes the field.

Risk: low - changes are additive and behind feature flags in CI. No runtime code touching serving path.

Migration: none required; reporting pipeline v111 coexists with previous versions and is opt-in via config.
